newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee retains losses, New York choppy.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee retains losses, New York choppy.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures retained most of their losses by the close on Thursday with the market finding little impetus from choppy New York arabica futures, traders said.
Benchmark September filled a chart gap at between $1,615 and $1,640 a tonne and ended the day at $1,636, off $35.
Spot month July expired at $1,610 for a $46 loss.
Traders said September needed to close above $1,680 to help boost the technical outlook.
"At $1,640, it would be just mildly constructive," said one.
Volume stood at just 3,295 lots. The Sept/Nov switch traded at $10.
New York arabica futures, which saw an eleventh-hour speculative sell-off on Wednesday, turned choppy in nervous trading, pressured by commission house selling.

Elsewhere, traders noted a report from Brazil which quoted official sources as pegging the 1997/98 (April-May) Brazil coffee crop at 20 million bags, down from the 22 million forecast by the Industry and Commerce Ministry earlier this year.
But the Brazilian government on Thursday maintained that it had not changed its forecast of 22 million bags.
"Despite the private sector predicting a crop as low as 18 million bags, we stick to our projection of a crop of 22 million," the interim head of the National Coffee Department, Roberto Abreu, said.
